_readme: Operator corrections to the broker's grouping, and decisions about them.
This file is committed and hash-chained -- it is copied into the record and
its digest is pinned by every session snapshot, so a correction cannot be
made without the chain showing it.
split:    [trade_id, ...]                    one trade -> one per leg
reviewed: {trade_id: reason}                 looked at it; it stands
On the four trades the grouper flagged: all four are RE-ENTRIES, not
scale-ins, and are correctly counted as separate trades. The position was
flat between each pair -- 115 seconds on 08-11, 6 seconds on 08-13 -- and a
position you are not in cannot be scaled into. The linkage rules cannot see
intent, so they flag proximity and ask; this is the answer.
Worth stating because it runs the other way: merging both pairs would have
RAISED the published return, from +1.1310% to +1.2850%. Two 1-NQ trades
each carry their full standardised P&L, while one 2-NQ trade carries half
the combined figure -- and the 08-13 pair holds a -429.50 loser whose weight
merging would have halved. The treatment kept here is both the correct one
